body: Yes, please do a confirm and close pass now.

anchor.quote: /guardrails-review has no probe for two same-tier tasks sharing a writeScope

body: File this and add it as part of #201 arc in the appropriate order.
Yes, if you think that we should do it now, that is great.  Otherwise, file an issue and put in #201 to address in the appropriate order of sequence.
But this is still for scope of #201.  Right?  Also, please file an issue that is deferred for v2, for a runner in Codex.

Done — all three verified in the tree first, then closed with the evidence in the closing comment rather than a bare 'done'. #224 (registry, three axes, providers init), #225 (both halves, including the not-configured gate that writes zero tier bytes), #226 (static resolver at DoR 10's v1 scope; probe-informed resolution stays #227). Each close also names what it does NOT cover, so the next reader is not misled the other way: #224 leaves GR2051-2053, #225 leaves #229, #226 leaves #349.

Filed as #493 (priority: medium) and added to the #201 sub-issue index with an explicit sequencing note. On 'the appropriate order' I did not just append it: its natural slot is BEFORE this stage runs, because Stage 3's whole wave structure was hand-designed around that hazard precisely because nothing checks it - landing the probe first would let it verify the hand-design rather than confirm it retrospectively. Against that, it delays Stage 3 and the structure is already deliberate. I wrote both sides into the epic and left the call to you rather than picking. The issue also records the measured cost (Stage 1: run abort, corrupted SSOT, ~$20) and why #458 makes that shape a guaranteed halt now rather than a likely one.

Did it now - it was one grep, and the answer is that the gap is already CLOSED and the note recording it was stale. GR2043 InvalidTierValue now covers all FOUR tier-bearing sites, not two: PlanValidator.cs:465 (plan default), :473 (tiering.verifier.minTier), :487 (action.tier), :498 (judge frontmatter tier). Stage 2 landed both of the two the note called 'not parsed at all'; minTier parses at PlanLoader.cs:222. GR2047-GR2050 shipped as well, so of the seven codes 13.3 lists as unimplemented only this stage's three remain. So: no issue filed, nothing to sequence. I added a dated STATUS UPDATE block to DoR 13.3 rather than rewriting the section, per its own 'recorded, not silently fixed' discipline. Worth noting the shape - that note was true when written and false when read, with nothing in between to say so. That is the same defect class this whole stage is about, and this time it was in our own design document.

Yes - still #201, and you were right to challenge the wording. 'Also out' read as 'out of the epic' when it meant 'out of Stage 3'. Rewritten: the Scope section now opens with a note saying 'out' here never means out of the epic, and the two lists are relabelled 'Still #201, deferred to v2' and 'Still #201, but not on this stage's path'. The only genuinely-outside-#201 item is #493, and it now says so explicitly with the reason. Codex runner filed as #494, v2, priority low. I kept it SEPARATE from #223 deliberately: both fill the DoR 4.4 kind seam, but #223 waits on local hardware being available to test against and a Codex CLI runner does not - sequencing them together would strand the one that is not blocked behind the one that is. #494 also records a trap worth knowing before anyone builds it: 6.5 rule 4 reads kind != 'claude' as weak-unless-declared, so a Codex block with no explicit strength gets treated as weak whenever it judges.
